title: Hearing Jimmy Blanton and playing pizzicato solos
summary: He says Blanton showed how the bass should be played, unlike Slam Stewart's bowing, and that he followed him around.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Who was the first bass player you ever heard take solos -- Jazz solos?
Well, I used to play solos, you know, mostly melodic solos. But the most impressive bass player that I heard has to be Jimmy Blanton.
When you first heard him, what did you think?

Well, I said, 'This is the way the bass is supposed to be played.' And I'm sure he inspired all of us. Although prior to that time, I had been playing solos, but nothing like Blanton. He was unbelievable. And there was Slam Stewart, who specialized with the bowed solos. But that was never my thing. My bowing was in the symphony and legitimate type music. I always preferred to play pizzicato solos.
And you say yours weren't anything like his. How would you differentiate what you were playing from what you heard Jimmy Blanton playing?
